idea.title: The buyer messaged 3 agents. Who won?
idea.angle: I tell it from the buyer's side: she sees a city apartment, messages three agents, and books with whoever answers first. Speed often beats the best listing.

slides.heading: SHE MESSAGED **3 AGENTS**. WHO WON?
slides.body: Not the one with the best listing.

slides.heading: SHE FINDS A CITY **APARTMENT**
slides.body: Say she sees three similar 2-bed apartments, from three agents. She likes all of them. So she messages all three.

slides.heading: REPLIES THE **NEXT DAY**
slides.body: A long, friendly message. Great photos too. But she has already booked a viewing somewhere else.

slides.heading: REPLIES IN **3 HOURS**
slides.body: "Yes, it's available." Nothing more. By then she already has a viewing time from someone else.

slides.heading: REPLIES IN **MINUTES**
slides.body: Confirms the apartment, shares the basics and offers Saturday at 10. She says yes. This agent wins.

slides.heading: YOU DID THE HARD PART. THEN **LOST** HER.
slides.body: Your post worked. She messaged you. A slow reply handed her to another agent.

slides.heading: SPEED OFTEN BEATS THE **BEST** LISTING.
slides.body: Decide now who replies, and how fast.

slides.heading: BE THE AGENT WHO **REPLIES** FIRST
slides.body: Comment LISTING and I'll send you the playbook

caption:
She messaged three agents about the same kind of apartment. Only one got the viewing.

It wasn't the agent with the best photos.
It was the one who answered first, with the basics and a viewing time.
A buyer who waits hours has usually messaged other agents by then.
More enquiries only matter if someone answers fast.

Comment LISTING and I'll send you the playbook.
